b2-57.title: In the newsroom
b2-57.story: Anna spent a week of work experience at a national [[broadcaster]] in Kyiv. On her first morning, the [[newsroom]] was louder than she had expected. Her job was to prepare a short news [[digest]] for the station's website. At lunch, a [[tabloid]] published a story about a [[scandal]] involving a famous football coach. Everyone wanted to report it, but the chief editor asked them to check the facts first. A [[correspondent]] in Lviv called and confirmed that the rumors were false. That evening, the editor wrote an [[editorial]] about why the [[mass media]] should not repeat gossip. Anna shared it on social [[media]], and Max replied, "Best first week ever!"

b2-58.title: Learning to code
b2-58.story: Max wanted to build a small [[bot]] that answers questions about his school timetable. His sister Sofia, a [[software engineer]], offered to help him on Saturday. First, she explained that every [[programmer]] makes mistakes, so he shouldn't panic. They wrote a simple [[algorithm]] that finds the next lesson for any day. Max tested it, but the [[output]] was always "Monday, 8:00." Sofia opened the [[log]] and found the problem: the program ignored the user's [[input]]. After fixing it, they designed a clean [[interface]] with two big buttons. Max even wrote a short [[manual]] so his classmates would know how to use it. By evening, his friends were sending it questions, and [[coding]] suddenly seemed much less scary.

b2-59.title: Building a computer
b2-59.story: Max decided to build his own computer instead of buying a new one. Anna's dad, who loves electronics, offered to help him choose each [[component]]. They spent an hour comparing prices for a [[processor]] and a graphics card. Dad explained that a modern [[chip]] contains billions of tiny switches. "Each [[transistor]] is smaller than a virus," he said. He also reminded Max that a single [[byte]] is made up of eight bits. The power supply was rated at 650 [[watts|watt]], which was enough for everything. When they finally turned it on, Max checked his [[ping]] and was delighted with the result. That night, he paid for cheap [[hosting]] and started planning a [[redesign]] of his old gaming blog.

b2-60.title: A night of gaming
b2-60.story: On Friday night, Lisa and Ira came to Anna's place for a gaming marathon. Ira had downloaded a [[mod]] that turned all the monsters into giant ducks. "[[LOL]], this is the best thing ever," Lisa wrote in the group chat. Around midnight, a strange message appeared, claiming that a [[hacker]] had taken over their account. Anna immediately texted Max's sister Sofia, who works in [[high-tech]]. Sofia replied that it was just a fake pop-up from a browser [[plug-in]]. She explained that real [[hacking]] rarely looks so dramatic. The girls deleted it and went back to their ducks. At three in the morning, the screen finally showed "[[game over]]," and everyone fell asleep on the sofa.

b2-61.title: Computer problems
b2-61.story: On Monday morning, Anna's laptop seemed to have a mind of its own. First, the [[touchpad]] stopped responding, and the [[cursor]] froze in the corner of the screen. She plugged in a mouse, but her [[login]] was rejected three times. Then she noticed that [[caps lock]] was on, so every password she typed was wrong. Once she got in, a single [[misclick]] almost deleted her history essay. She pressed [[print screen]] to save the error message and sent it to Max. He told her to run the [[antivirus]] and do a full [[restart]]. It worked, and even her [[screensaver]] with the family dog came back. Later, she discovered that the [[spam filter]] had hidden Max's long email full of tips.

b2-62.title: Shopping online
b2-62.story: Anna's mama had a birthday coming up, so Anna decided to shop online. After an hour of [[scrolling]], she found a lovely scarf already saved on her [[wishlist]]. The store was new, and Lisa had sent her an [[invite code]] for a discount. However, the discount didn't appear when she tried to pay. Anna clicked the [[live chat]] button, but only a [[chatbot]] answered, with useless replies. Finally, a real assistant explained that she had forgotten to tick a [[checkbox]] under the code. With one [[swipe]], she confirmed the payment on her phone. Two days later, mama opened the parcel and loved the scarf.

b2-63.title: Playing video games
b2-63.story: Taras got a [[gamepad]] for his birthday, and Max promised to teach him a flying game. The [[joystick]] felt strange at first, and Taras kept crashing his plane into mountains. His first attempt was an [[epic fail]], but he refused to give up. Max showed him a popular [[streamer]] who explains the game clearly. During her [[livestream]], she shared a [[cheat code]] for extra fuel, but Max said real pilots don't cheat. After two hours of practice, Taras managed to [[level up]] three times. Then they tried [[multiplayer]] together against kids from all over the world. By the end of the evening, Taras's name appeared on the weekly [[leaderboard]], and he proudly sent a photo of it to grandma.

b2-64.title: Life on social media
b2-64.story: Last week, Ira posted a video of her dog stealing a sandwich from the table. By the next morning, it had become an [[internet meme]] that everyone at school was sharing. Anna's [[repost]] alone got hundreds of likes, and the original collected thousands of [[retweets|retweet]]. Then someone shared an old clip of Ira singing with a silly [[photo filter]] on her face. Ira laughed and admitted it was pure [[cringe]]. Soon, however, a [[bot account]] and a few classmates began posting nasty comments under every post she made. Anna knew this was [[cyberbullying]], so she reported the comments and told their teacher. When the class chat filled up with jokes about it, Max politely asked everyone to move the [[off-topic]] to another group. Meanwhile, Ira's dad found good advice on an [[internet forum]], and by Friday the comments had stopped.
